generation_contract.dialogue_ids: campaign metadata; RCT sidecars require a future compiler

trainers.strategy: Geodude establishes rocks and speed control; Cranidos breaks; Onix converts a super-effective hit into a Weakness Policy counterattack.
trainers.ace_math_change: Sturdy guarantees one action; Weakness Policy turns the expected Water or Grass hit into a damage race.

trainers.strategy: Horsea starts rain; Lombre exploits it; Lightning Rod Goldeen disrupts a single Electric sweep; Starmie closes with broad special coverage.
trainers.ace_math_change: Life Orb makes Starmie's neutral coverage materially stronger while rain changes Water damage and turn order.

trainers.strategy: Electabuzz establishes paralysis and a screen; Magnezone pivots; Boltund attacks the resistance core; Air Balloon Raichu denies the first Ground line.
trainers.ace_math_change: Air Balloon forces the player to spend a turn breaking the ace's Ground immunity before cashing in the route's main answer.

availability_contract.failure: Only Bunnelby/Diggersby is a dependable ambient Ground family; the proposed Route 2 Geodude quarry is not implemented.

trainers.strategy: Bellossom starts sun and sleep pressure; Roserade lays hazards; Victreebel breaks under sun; Coba Berry Vileplume survives one Flying answer and sets up.
trainers.ace_math_change: Coba Berry removes the certainty of a one-hit Flying knockout and gives Growth a plausible opening.

trainers.strategy: Crobat creates Tailwind; Weezing blocks easy Ground lines; Drapion lays poison hazards; Toxtricity breaks; Venomoth snowballs through Tinted Lens.
trainers.ace_math_change: Tinted Lens makes normal Bug resists unreliable after Quiver Dance, demanding speed control or priority rather than type alone.

trainers.strategy: Hatterene reverses speed with Trick Room; Mr. Mime disrupts; Bronzong sustains the room; Rapidash breaks; Magic Guard Alakazam ignores passive damage.
trainers.ace_math_change: Magic Guard removes Life Orb recoil, so Alakazam gets the damage increase without the usual clock.

availability_contract.failure: A second broad answer depends on the unproven haunted-mansion Habitat; do not count it until runtime-proven.

trainers.strategy: Drought Torkoal sets hazards and sun; Arcanine pressures physical answers; Magcargo punishes passivity; Magmortar and Typhlosion break; Charizard exploits sun.
trainers.ace_math_change: Solar Power plus sun changes damage thresholds, while Power Herb lets Charizard fire one immediate Solar Beam even if weather is displaced.

trainers.strategy: Roster intentionally withheld until the singles-versus-doubles decision is settled.
Snow, hazards and speed denial make resource preservation matter across the whole fight.
trainers.ace_math_change: Assault Vest turns Lapras into a special sponge while Freeze-Dry reverses the usual Water counter.

trainers.strategy: Fake Out, removal, priority and mixed physical pressure punish a team that reaches the League without tempo tools.
trainers.ace_math_change: White Herb restores the defense drops from Close Combat and consumes itself to activate Unburden.

trainers.strategy: Burns, Taunt, Trick and priority deny clean setup and force the player to manage status across six different Ghost patterns.
trainers.ace_math_change: Focus Sash guarantees Gengar a response and makes priority or prior hazard control part of the answer.

trainers.strategy: Aerodactyl sets the pace, each midgame member attacks a different Dragon answer, and Dragonite is the only dedicated setup closer.
trainers.ace_math_change: Multiscale plus Weakness Policy punishes an undisciplined super-effective first hit and changes priority damage thresholds.

trainers.strategy: Blue recombines the campaign's lessons: tempo lead, sleep, hazards, Intimidate, speed, and a setup ace with no single type shortcut.
trainers.ace_math_change: White Herb erases Shell Smash's defensive cost, forcing the player to stop the setup or answer a full-speed mixed-coverage closer.
